newsitem.title: USA: Johnson & Johnson swaps drug brands with Pharmacia.
newsitem.headline: Johnson & Johnson swaps drug brands with Pharmacia.

text.p: Some of the best-known over-the-counter drugs will carry different makers' names following a product swap announced Thursday by Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc. and Johnson & Johnson.

The two companies are among the world's largest drug manufacturers but consumers are unlikely to notice any changes in the prices or packaging of the brands exchanged in the deal, industry analysts said.
"Most people don't even bother to pick up the package and read who makes it anyway," said Brian Eisenbarth at Collins & Co., a San Francisco-area brokerage and investment bank.

J&J, the maker of Tylenol, acquired Motrin in the deal. Being able to sell both will enable J&J to offer "the most comprehensive range of analgesic options for adults and children of any company in the world," said Brian Perkins, president of J&J's McNeil Consumer Products subsidiary.
J&J, based in Brunswick, N.J., also gained control of Mycitracin, an antibiotic ointment, in the swap.

In exchange, J&J gave Pharmacia & Upjohn three products: Nasalcrom, a nasal spray for hay fever; PediaCare, a line of children's cough and cold products, and Micatin, an anti-fungal application for athlete's foot.

"This trade is an outstanding opportunity to expand and strengthen our portfolio," said Michael Valentino, president of Pharmacia Consumer Healthcare U.S. "It makes sense for both parties, with each benefiting from strong brand heritage."

The brand exchange did not include an exchange of cash or other considerations, said a spokesman for Swedish-American Pharmacia & Upjohn, which is based in London. Its U.S. operations are based in Kalamazoo, Mich.
"All these products have been declining for some time. This is pretty small stuff for these companies," said Hemant Shah, an independent industry analyst in New Jersey.
J&J stock rose 12.5 cents to $59.50 and Pharmacia also rose 12.5 cents to $34.875, both in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
